rules.title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords, and management companies must give tenants the City's Tenants Rights and Resources Guide when a tenancy begins (at lease signing or first rent payment) and when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken, such as a notice to quit or summary process. The Guide does not have to be given at each lease renewal.
rules.key_value: Guide required at start and termination of tenancy; $300/day fine
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including tenants at will and single rental units in owner-occupied buildings; all tenants and lawful occupants must receive the materials.
rules.exemptions: Rental units in hospitals, skilled nursing facilities or health facilities; non-profit facilities whose primary purpose is short-term substance abuse treatment; Short Term Rental Units under Article 4, Section 4.60 of the Cambridge Zoning Ordinance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Excludes hospital/health/skilled nursing facility units, non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities, and short-term rental units.

rules.penalty: Fine of $300 for each day's violation (Sec. 8.71.070).
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.
rules.conflict_note: The page does not state an effective date; it was first posted 10/14/2020. The ordinance does not restrict grounds for eviction; it is a notice requirement categorized under just_cause_eviction.
